beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: The rain has stopped the party for the evening. There is a fire, and it is holding, and there is nothing to do until morning.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: We should settle the watch order before it gets too late.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: I have some opinions on how the fire was laid, if anyone's interested.

beats.speaker: Vigil
beats.text: The fire will last the night.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: leena: Do you think the rain will stop by morning?

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: The rain does not stop. The conversation fades into silence as the group settles in for the night.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: The endless road stretches before the party, surrounded by nothing but open land and the occasional tree.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: Vabokedos, my home, is a place of peace and serenity. A land of rolling hills and crystal-clear lakes.

beats.speaker: Vigil
beats.text: Nafsari... it's a place I once called home. But no more.

beats.speaker: Leena
beats.text: My village is a special place, filled with kind-hearted people and bountiful fields. A true paradise on earth.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Enough about our pasts. Let's focus on the journey ahead.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: The road continues on, an unending path to their uncertain future.

beats.speaker: Leena
beats.text: You ever notice how quiet it gets out here?

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: Chadwick: Yeah. Hard to believe there's anyone else alive sometimes.

beats.speaker: Leena
beats.text: S'pose that's why we're out here. No one to bother us.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: Chadwick: Except the ones we're botherin' ourselves.

beats.speaker: Leena
beats.text: You ever think maybe they don't need us watchin'?

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: Chadwick: Probably not. But I'd rather be safe than sorry.

beats.speaker: Leena
beats.text: S'pose so. You ever look at the stars and wonder what you're doin' here?

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: Chadwick: All the time. Don't think I've ever figured it out though.

beats.speaker: Leena
beats.text: Me neither. But maybe that's okay.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: The party sits around a crackling fire, the smell of burnt stew wafting through the air.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: This stew is an atrocity. I could make a dish ten times better with my eyes closed.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Can we just... not do this? Not every meal has to be a production.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: leena: It's not that bad, really. Let's just enjoy the company and the warmth of the fire.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: vigil: I'm not really hungry anyway. Here, Sodacan Bob, you have my portion.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: Sodacan Bob has stopped in his tracks, his eyes wide with excitement as he examines a rusty old wagon axle lying in the dirt.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: Look at this! Do you know where this was made? In the northern provinces, by a skilled craftsman. See the maker's mark? It's worn, but still visible.

beats.speaker: Leena
beats.text: Really? That's fascinating, Sodacan Bob. What can you tell us about the craftsman?

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Can we please keep moving? We've got a job to do, remember?

beats.speaker: Vigil
beats.text: How long ago was it made, would you say?

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: Oh, at least 50 years ago, if not more. The design is quite old-fashioned. This axle has seen a lot of use.

beats.speaker: Leena
beats.text: It's incredible that it's survived this long. What do you think it's been through?

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: Well, the wear patterns suggest it was used heavily for many years, likely on rough terrain. The rusting is consistent with exposure to the elements over decades.

beats.speaker: Vigil
beats.text: That's really interesting. Thank you for sharing all that, Sodacan Bob.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Can we go now?

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: We've been walking for hours, and I still don't recognize anything.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: leena: Maybe we should consult the map, just to be sure.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: vigil: I know exactly where we are, but I'll wait until someone asks.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: This is hilarious! Chadwick's so lost, but he won't admit it!

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: leena: You know, Chadwick, even the greatest leaders need help sometimes.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: I don't need help! I know where we're going!

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: Sure, keep telling yourself that, Chadwick.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: vigil: (quietly to Leena) Should I tell him? Or will that make it worse?

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: leena: Let's give him a little more time. He might ask for help himself.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: I can't wait to see what happens next! This is better than any story!

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Two hours each. I take first watch. Sodacan Bob, second. Vigil, third. Leena, you sleep through.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: "I'll take second, but I'm telling you

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: The onion went in before the oil was hot. You can taste it. That's not seasoning, that's a mistake.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: leena: We are together. There is enough. And that is the whole point of a table.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Mm. Yes. I'm done.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: vigil: — Take this. I don't want it.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: I would have rendered the fat first. I could cook in your sleep, Chadwick.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Nobody asked. Put your fork down, Sodacan Bob.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: leena: The pot. We need to agree who is scrubbing the pot. It was not clean last time.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Eat. Everyone eat. No more.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: Look at this. Look at the truing on the axle — see how the hammer marks

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: Northeast. I can feel the pull in the ground. We walk northeast.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: Oh, good. That's the third 'northeast' in a mile. I'm sure the ground is very flattered.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: vigil: "It's southeast, for the record. But yes. You are heading... in the right direction."

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: leena: "Maybe we just pause a moment, check the map, confirm your read on the—

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: I don't need the map. I need you to trust the man holding the stick.

beats.speaker: sodacan_bob
beats.text: He's holding a stick. It's a stick. It has never once pointed anywhere, Chadwick.

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: The stick is pointed. That is directional data. We walk. We arrive. End of sentence.

beats.speaker: gm
beats.text: vigil: "Right. We walk. ...Southeast, in case the stick changes its mind."

beats.speaker: chadwick
beats.text: The stick does not change its mind. We arrive. I said end of sentence.
